newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Three senior S.African Telkom officials resign.
newsitem.headline: Three senior S.African Telkom officials resign.

text.p: Three top officials from South Africa's Telkom had resigned ahead of the partial privatisation of the telecommunications utility, Telkom chairman Dikgang Moseneke told state radio.
Moseneke said all three officials would be replaced by specialists from the Malaysian-U.S. consortium which bought a 30 percent stake in Telkom, announced in March this year.
Telkom Malaysia Bhd partnered by U.S-based SBC Communications Inc bought the Telkom stake for $1.261 billion (5.58 billion rand).
"All three will be replaced by Americans or Malaysians, so their departure comes because there are in fact specialists who have been appointed in each of those slots," Moseneke said.
The three officials to be replaced are Telkom's financial executive Angus Band, head of networks, Hannes Steyn, and head of Information Technology, Peter Jordi.
"We've made job offers to them and we still repeat our position...no person whatsoever will lose his or her job on account of the introduction of the SBC and Malaysian Telekom people," he added.
Moseneke said the three officials had chosen not to accept other job offers within Telkom.
"Because they are being replaced directly they chose not to accept other job offers within Telkom," he added.
Only one other senior Telkom official, managing director Brian Clark, resigned on April 30 after the partial privatisation had been confirmed.
The privatisation deal is the biggest direct investment in South Africa yet, and the inflows from the deal will be closely monitored by the South African Reserve Bank.

The cash is expected to flow into the money market within the next three months. Officials say the money will be paid by the consortium acquiring the 30 percent stake on finalisation of the deal expected within 90 days of the signing on March 26.
